scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: This foundation was begun 1441 on a small site, now the Old Schools.

scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: It had a small chapel, which was begun in 1444.

scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: The first stone of the Chapel was laid, by Henry himself, on the Feast of St James the Apostle, 25 July 1446.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: The Chapel was built in phases by a succession of kings of England from 1448 to 1515, a period which spanned the Wars of the Roses and three subsequent decades.

scenes.title: History
scenes.caption: However, Henry soon greatly expanded his scheme, demolishing a large swathe of the town to begin a large court and chapel, the dimensions of which were specified  in his Will and Intent of 12 March 1448.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: The Chapel's large stained glass windows were completed by 1531, and its early Renaissance pulpitum was erected in 1532–36.
